provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Marks the place a movement is aimed at and ends at (東京に戻る, あの店に行く), the same slot へ fills, though に stresses arrival where へ stresses direction. Sibling lanes take the point where something simply is (駅の裏にある), the purpose of a trip rather than its goal (買い物に行く), and the person told something (親に言う). にゃ is the casual contraction of には, so it adds は's contrast and is limited to speech and fiction dialogue.

examples.ruby: あんな店[みせ]にゃ二度[にど]と行[い]かないと決[き]めた。
examples.english: I've decided I'm never setting foot in that place again.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の朝[あさ]は東京[とうきょう]にゃ戻[もど]っているはずだ。
examples.english: I should be back in Tokyo by tomorrow morning, anyway.

examples.ruby: 山[やま]の上[うえ]の神社[じんじゃ]にゃ、車[くるま]では行[い]けないよ。
examples.english: You can't get up to the shrine on the mountain by car, at any rate.

patterns.usage_note: Marks the direction or endpoint of movement, and by extension the person a message or thing is headed for: 大阪へ出張する, 山田様へ. に pins down arrival at the goal, while へ typically keeps the focus on the heading, which is why it is the usual choice on envelopes and dedications. Unlike its class-mate にゃ it is neutral in register and normal in writing.

examples.ruby: 来週[らいしゅう]の月曜[げつよう]に大阪[おおさか]へ出張[しゅっちょう]します。
examples.english: I'm heading to Osaka on business next Monday.

examples.ruby: 子[こ]どもたちが公園[こうえん]へ駆[か]け出[だ]していった。
examples.english: The kids went tearing off toward the park.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい住所[じゅうしょ]を旧友[きゅうゆう]へ葉書[はがき]で知[し]らせた。
examples.english: I sent an old friend a postcard with my new address.
